corrections.caveats: The README and CHANGELOG of frerich/clcache carry no timing numbers (only 'greatly improves performance of cache hits' for the server). The only reachable numbers are third-party CI anecdotes. The OpenMW merge request (opened 2025-11-29) used Aussiemon's fork pinned to a commit, not upstream, and states no uncached time (only that it is near the 2 hour timeout), no runner hardware, and mixes cache states across different pipeline runs, so the speedup is approximate and not a controlled comparison. The upstream issue https://github.com/frerich/clcache/issues/251 (2016, Windows Server 2012 R2, E5-2650) reports the opposite: a 5 to 8 minute build rose to 23 minutes with a cold cache and was roughly equal to no clcache when fully cached, blamed on cache lock contention and virus scanning. The same MR author found ccache's MSVC precompiled-header hits as slow as misses and called clcache the most stable option, but wished ccache could match its speed. [verifier] As of the check, MR !5021 is still a Draft and not merged into OpenMW master; its first clcache run (empty cache) also hit the timeout, and the fork patches clcache for Python >=3.10 and MSVC >=2019, so upstream clcache itself was not what was timed.

corrections.caveats: Neither the sccache README nor docs carry timing numbers. The reachable figures are one third-party CI pull request (opened and merged 2026-10-16) with a mixed Rust plus C++ workload, no runner hardware, compiler or sccache version stated, 219 sccache write errors from GitHub cache throttling, and the uncached run being a different pipeline run than the cached ones; the gain comes mostly from C/C++ objects already cached on main. Against ccache, the only measurement found is the repo's own issue https://github.com/mozilla/sccache/issues/160 (2017, Firefox clobber build with Clang 4.0.0 on Ubuntu 17.04, hardware not stated), where fully cached ccache took 35 s wall versus 107 s wall for sccache's local disk cache (3 to 4.5 times slower); the issue was closed in February 2024 as 'should be good now' without new measurements, so sccache has no evidence of beating ccache here. [verifier] In the same issue, ccache with compression = true and direct_mode = false took 96 s wall, so much of ccache's lead came from its direct mode. The PR's table also lists four other uncached main runs with doc-review steps of 763 to 1,062 s, so the uncached baseline varies run to run.

notes: All PR numbers and hit/miss stats match (17m26s, 6m23s, 2m46s; 1,425/711/478 s; 1,803/319 C/C++, 10/223 Rust; 219 write errors). Last commit 2026-10-24, Apache-2.0, 7.8k stars confirmed. Ratios are correctly marked derived.
